Coercion and Defaults

Every route param and query value is a string — z.coerce fixes that as part of validating it, not after.

Lesson 2's defensive Number(req.params.id) (Figure 2.16) is still true here for exactly the same reason: Express route params, and every query-string value, always arrive as strings — /tickets/7 gives req.params.id === '7', never the number 7. A validator that only checked z.number().int().positive() against that string would reject every single request, since '7' isn't a JS number at all.

// Figure 3.6: coercing strings into the types they actually mean (src/validators/ticket.validators.js, excerpt)
export const ticketIdParamSchema = z.object({
  id: z.coerce.number().int().positive(),
});

export const listTicketsQuerySchema = z.object({
  status: statusEnum.optional(),
  sortBy: z.enum(['createdAt', 'updatedAt', 'subject', 'status']).default('createdAt'),
  order: z.enum(['asc', 'desc']).default('desc'),
  page: z.coerce.number().int().min(1).default(1),
  pageSize: z.coerce.number().int().min(1).max(50).default(10),
});

z.coerce.number() converts before checking — it runs Number(...) on whatever it's given, then validates the result, so '7' passes and becomes the number 7 in result.data, while 'seven' becomes NaN and correctly fails .int().positive(). That single change replaces the manual Number.isNaN(id) guard from Lesson 2 entirely: it's now something the schema itself expresses, not a follow-up check after the fact.

(statusEnum, defined just above this excerpt in the same file, is a plain z.enum([...]) of the four values Ticket.status can hold — the same kind of allow-list check as sortBy/order below it.)

.default(...) handles the other half of listTicketsQuerySchema: a bare GET /tickets with no query string at all is still a completely valid request — it should just mean "first page, ten at a time, newest first." page: z.coerce.number()...default(1) means an absent page doesn't fail validation, it becomes exactly 1 in the parsed result. Combined with validate.js replacing req.query with that parsed data (previous slide), every route reading req.query.page downstream can trust it's always a real number, defaulted or not — never undefined, never a string.
